Grazing traditionally started on Saint George's Day, the 6th of May. It was a holiday for the entire village. The shepherd asked owners not to be late, or he refused to graze their cattle. The owners drove their animals with pussy-willow branches leftover from Easter. When the herd was gathered, the shepherd walked around it clockwise holding an icon and reciting prayers. Sometimes, during the third round he cast a special shepherd's spell.
按照传统，5月6日的圣格里高利日是开始放牧的日子，这是整个村庄的节日。牛羊倌会要求牲口主人准时交接，不然就拒绝帮他们放牧。主人用复活节剩下的柳枝驱赶牲口，牧群聚到一起之后，牧人会一边抱着圣像顺时针走，一边祷告。牧人有时转第三圈的时候还会施放特殊的牧人咒语。
en

Kupala Night (also called Ivanа-Kupala) is a Christian variant of a pagan rite that took place on the summer solstice of June 24th (July 7th, New Style). The Orthodox variant is meant to coincide with John the Baptist's birthday, but the holiday has stayed pagan in essence. People prayed to John (Ivan) the Baptist to relieve headaches and bless their children. 
On the morning of "Ivan", people prepared a wholegrain porridge – kutia. They did so on all the other transition cycle holidays, on days that opened the borders between worlds. Slavic paganism probably had no specific deity by the name of Kupala, which is simply a folk variant of the name John the Baptist. After all, children were baptized by being dipped in the closest body of water or in a baptismal font ("kupel" in Russian).

库帕拉之夜（也叫伊万·库帕拉节）是某一异教仪式融入基督教之后形成的节日，通常是在6月24日（新历7月7日）夏至。东正教库帕拉之夜之所以选这一天，是为了和施洗者圣约翰的生日重合，但这个节日本质上始终保有异教的色彩。人们向施洗者圣约翰（伊万）祈祷，以求治愈头痛和保佑他们的孩子。
在“伊万”的早晨，人们会煮库提亚这种全麦粥。其他周期转换的节日以及两界边界开放的日子，他们也会煮这道粥。斯拉夫异教可能没有哪个神祇名叫库帕拉，这只是施洗者圣约翰的民间称谓。毕竟，孩童接受洗礼的方式就是浸入最近的水体或洗礼池（俄语叫“库佩尔”）。
